title: Number of Different Subsequences GCDs
summary: Given an array of positive integers, calculate the total number of distinct greatest common divisors (GCDs) that can be obtained from all possible non-empty subsequences of the array.
statement: Given an array of positive integers, calculate the total number of distinct greatest common divisors (GCDs) that can be obtained from all possible non-empty subsequences of the array.
constraints: Consider every nonempty subsequence and count distinct resulting greatest common divisors.
hints: A candidate g is achievable exactly when the GCD of all present multiples of g equals g.
Store input values in a set and scan multiples for each candidate.
Accumulate their GCD and stop as soon as it reaches the candidate.
Every subsequence producing g contains only multiples of g; conversely, the collected multiples themselves form a subsequence with GCD g when their common GCD reaches g.
editorial: Every subsequence producing g contains only multiples of g; conversely, the collected multiples themselves form a subsequence with GCD g when their common GCD reaches g.

tests.explanation: The achievable GCD values are 1,2,3,6,10, giving five.
The distinct subsequence GCDs total seven.
